newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS - Lend Lease posts steady gain.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS - Lend Lease posts steady gain.

text.p: Property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp Ltd posted another steady rise in half year earnings on Thursday, with managing director David Higgins tipping another rise in full year earnings.
"We thought the result was one of the most straight forward we've had in ages," Higgins told reporters.
Net profit rose 14.2 percent to a neat A$160 million, towards the upper end of analysts' forecasts of between A$155 million to A$162 million.
The two key divisions, financial services and property services, both recorded steady profit growth of 9.2 percent and 8.3 percent, respectively.

"Financial services businesses achieved sales of A$1.4 billion (in the half), with retail sales increasing by 52 percent over December 1995 reflecting positive investment markets," Lend Lease said in a statement.
Higgins said the company's very low debt to equity ratio of 2.8 percent as at December 31 put it in a good position to take advantage of acquisition opportunities.
Turning to Asia, Higgins said Lend Lease was making steady inroads into property markets there, but warned some sectors were showing signs of overheating.
"Who knows how high the commercial market in Hong Kong is going to go? It went up 50 percent in the last 12 months. We thought that's enough, so we're out of Hong Kong now," he said.
The Thai property market had the right mix of economic and political features which attracted a company like Lend Lease, Higgins said.

Late on Thursday, Melbourne-based property group Hudson Conway Ltd said it and Lend Lease would bid jointly for both Melbourne's proposed Docklands sports stadium and the overall A$2 billion retail and residential redevelopment.
The company, which has a 30 percent interest in the Darling Park office project, said the inner Sydney complex had a strong outlook.
Units in the listed Darling Park trust have been disappointed investors, falling to 83 cents from their A$1.00 issue price.
In January, Lend Lease announced its first development in Thailand called Thai Markets in conjunction with the Modern Home Development Co Ltd.
The A$1 billion project is to develop an industrial, commercial and residential complex in northern Bangkok and Lend Lease's commitment is about A$100 million over four years.
Lend Lease shares closed 11 cents weaker at A$23.00 after rising early in response to the profit result.
